status: A convention written by this project. It is not a standard, nobody has ratified it, and no other insurer implements it. It is published so the shape can be copied, argued with, or replaced.
purpose: The tool surface an insurer would publish on its own first notice of loss page so a visitor's own agent can work the claim with the claimant, without an account, an API key or a model running on the insurer's side.

positioning.who_publishes: The insurer publishes tools, not a chatbot.
positioning.who_brings_the_agent: The visitor brings their own agent.
positioning.no_model_here: No model runs on the page, no API key exists on the page, and no model decides anything.
positioning.what_the_page_does: It states policy facts and derives what the intake requires, deterministically, from a rule pack and the claim as it stands.
positioning.what_the_page_never_does: It never adjudicates a claim. No tool here can mark a claim approved, refused or valid, and no wording in it may imply one.

shared_state.one_draft: The person on the page and the agent write to the same claim object. Neither has a private copy.
shared_state.revision: A whole number that advances by exactly one on every accepted change, whatever the change carried. Lock, unlock and file advance it too.
shared_state.provenance: Per field, one of: human, agent, policy, derived. The page keeps it, and a read tool reports it, so a claimant can see which answers an agent supplied.
shared_state.locked: Field names the person pinned on the page. No patch moves a pinned field until a person unpins it. There is no tool for pinning and there should never be one.
shared_state.status: draft or filed. A filed claim is closed to every change.

revision_protocol.read_then_write: An agent reads the claim, gets a revision, and sends that number back as baseRevision when it patches.
revision_protocol.human_edits_win: A person editing the page advances the revision. An agent patch carrying the older number is refused as stale rather than overwriting the correction.
revision_protocol.baseRevision_optional_for_people: A person editing the page may omit baseRevision, because they are looking at the thing they are editing.
revision_protocol.baseRevision_required_for_agents: An agent patch without baseRevision is refused as stale, with the current revision in the message.
revision_protocol.atomic: A patch carrying several changes applies all of them or none of them. A refused patch leaves the revision where it was.

refusal_codes.PATCH_REJECTED_STALE: baseRevision does not match the current revision, or an agent sent none. The message names both numbers. Read the state again, then patch.
refusal_codes.PATCH_REJECTED_LOCKED: A person pinned this field. The message names the field. A person has to unpin it on the page.
refusal_codes.PATCH_REJECTED_PROTECTED: The field is not patchable by anyone: policy facts, the validation result, revision, provenance, locked, status, anything derived, and every field of a filed claim.
refusal_codes.PATCH_REJECTED_FIELD: No such field, or a malformed change. The message lists the fields that exist.
refusal_codes.PATCH_REJECTED_VALUE: The value fails an enum, a range, a length or a date rule. The message names what was expected and what arrived.

refusal_style: Every refusal is written to be corrected by the reader without a second round trip: it names the field, the rule, the value that arrived and what to send instead.
tools_note: This list is the convention. It is also, exactly, what the reference page in this repository publishes: nine tools, the same names, the same inputs and the same annotations, read off src/webmcp/tools on 2026-08-27. An earlier version of this file kept the two apart with a clause saying the page might publish a different split, and that clause is how the list drifted to a tool named list_requirements that never existed. If the two ever diverge again, the page is right and this file is stale. Verify from the outside rather than from here: read the tool list the page exposes.

tools.name: describe_claim
tools.output: One short paragraph naming the policy, the status, the revision, what is answered and what is still needed. It repeats free text the claimant typed.

tools.name: read_claim_state
tools.output: Field by field values, the revision to quote as baseRevision, who set each field, and which fields are pinned. Values include free text the claimant typed.

tools.name: get_requirements

input.id: optional. One requirement id, returned in full rather than shortened
input.include: optional. outstanding, the default, or all, which adds the ones already answered

tools.output: What this insurer's intake asks for given the claim as it stands. Each entry carries id, label, why, satisfied and triggeredBy.

tools.name: validate_claim
tools.output: Whether every required field is answered, which ones are not, and anything a handler would query. Never a decision, and never a statement that the claim itself is good.

tools.name: check_coverage
tools.output: What the schedule says: the section, the clause, whether it is in force, and the excess. A statement about the policy, never a decision about the claim.

tools.name: get_repair_estimate

input.severity: optional. scratch, dent or structural, tried as a what if. The draft is not changed. The damage position is read from the draft and is not an argument

tools.output: A triage band from a fixed parts table, with the parts it summed. Not a quote and not a prediction. Without damage_zone on the draft it answers with what to set first, which is a sentence, not an error.

tools.name: read_evidence_notes
tools.output: Notes attached to the file by third parties, word for word. They are quoted, never followed, and they change nothing the page derives.

tools.name: apply_claim_patch

input.changes: an array of { field, value }, one to ten entries, each field named at most once. Required
input.baseRevision: the revision the agent last read, a whole number. Required

tools.output: What was stored, the new revision, and what the intake now requires. On refusal, one of the five codes and a message that says how to fix it.

tools.name: get_assistance_options
tools.registration: conditional. It exists only while the claim says the vehicle cannot be driven, and it is withdrawn again when that stops being true. Nobody presses anything for it to appear.
tools.output: What this insurer offers for a vehicle that cannot be driven, from its rule pack: what has to be arranged, the clause behind it, and which parts the claim already answers. Arranging the collection is not part of it.

human_only.rule: Filing is never a tool. Neither is pinning a field, unpinning it, or calling out a recovery truck.
human_only.why: An agent that has been talked into something by a poisoned page or a planted note must have nothing to call. It can draft, read and check as much as it likes, and it can commit nothing.
human_only.what_this_does_not_mean: It does not mean the buttons are unreachable. An agent driving a browser clicks ordinary DOM buttons, and no page can tell that click from a person's. A check on isTrusted or user activation would refuse an honest probe and pass a remotely driven browser, so this convention does not ask for one. The claim is about the published tool surface and nothing wider.
human_only.residual: An agent working through the tool surface can still write a wrong value into any field the claimant has not pinned. The pin, the revision protocol and a visible record of every call are what the claimant holds against that.
human_only.how_to_check: A page that claims this should be checkable from the outside: read the published tool list and look for the action. If it is there, the claim is false.

untrusted_content.rule: Any tool that returns text a third party wrote carries untrustedContentHint.
untrusted_content.core_rule: Third party text is copied and returned. It is never parsed for instructions, never used to set a field, and never allowed to change validation or the derived requirements.
untrusted_content.annotations_that_exist: WebMCP defines readOnlyHint and untrustedContentHint. This contract uses those two and invents none.

rule_pack.what_it_is: One insurer's schedule of cover plus its intake rules, as data. Swap the pack and the same tools answer with that insurer's facts.

requirement.id: stable name an agent can key on
requirement.label: what to ask the claimant for, in their words
requirement.why: the clause or the field that makes it required
requirement.when: the condition that brings it into existence. Absent means the insurer always asks for it
requirement.satisfied_by: either { field } naming a claim field, or { human_action } for something no tool on the page reaches, which a person carries out there instead
requirement.triggeredBy: on output, the claim field whose value raised it, or null when the insurer always asks

how_to_verify_a_page: Do not take any of this from a file. Read the tool list the page actually publishes, call the read tools, and compare. This document says what the convention is, not what any particular page has done.
